summary: A slide's two provider ordinals fence one operation attempt, not the slide's lifetime: when the fencing token advances the counter restarts and the calls already made move to provider_attempt_total.
invariants: Within one operation attempt a slide still admits at most two provider calls, and replaying the same ordinal stays idempotent.
Skipping or decreasing an ordinal inside an attempt still fails closed.
A stale worker holding an old attempt token still cannot advance the counter.
Calls spent in earlier attempts are preserved in provider_attempt_total for cost accounting.
Total provider calls for one slide stay bounded by the operation's own max_attempts.
forbidden: Treat the ordinal pair as a lifetime cap so a retry cannot re-author the slide that failed.
Reset the counter inside a single operation attempt.
rationale: Per-slide checkpoints already let a retry skip completed slides, so a one-slide failure never needed a whole new deck.

Measured on operation ce48036c: attempt 1 authored 34 of 35 slides in 15 minutes and slide 35 failed the header contract twice; attempt 2 reused the 34 checkpoints, found the slide's budget spent, and failed in 726 ms without calling the provider once.
The counter's purpose is a crash fence for one attempt -- do not pay twice for the same call after a lease takeover -- which an epoch preserves exactly.
